entities.summary: Edmund Beaufort, 2nd Duke of Somerset, was a pivotal English nobleman born around 1416 in England, whose rivalry with Richard, Duke of York, contributed to the outbreak of the Wars of the Roses. He played a crucial role in the Hundred Years' War, leading military campaigns on behalf of France and later becoming a key figure in the Lancastrian faction. His legacy extended to the establishment of the Order of the Garter, a prestigious chivalric order that continues to influence British culture to this day. Edmund Beaufort's impact on English history was marked by his strategic alliances and military victories, which ultimately led to his downfall and the rise of the Yorkist faction. He died on May 22, 1455, at the Battle of St Albans, leaving behind a legacy that would shape the course of English history for centuries to come.
